physiology:
The traditions seat this code in the solar plexus, the soft nerve cluster behind the belly, the dorsal ganglia that run alongside the spine and feel before the mind has formed a word for what is being felt. This is the body's first reader of a room. It tightens when something is off, it loosens when something is safe, and it does this whether you are paying attention or not. It is fitting that the code of family lives here, because family is the first place the belly learned what holding and not-holding felt like.

The shadow has its floor here. Weakness lives in a belly that has been told for too long that there is no one coming. The gut stays braced. Breath stays high in the chest. You stop being able to tell hunger from worry. Long enough in that posture and the body forgets it was ever meant to soften, and the soft part of you starts to look, even to yourself, like a flaw.

The climb is also here, and it is quieter than the climb of other codes. It is the belly remembering it can drop. It is one full breath into the lower abdomen, the kind that happens when someone trustworthy is nearby. The solar plexus does not heal by being addressed. It heals by being kept company.
amino_acid:
Deeper still, this code answers to a single amino acid, Proline. Proline is the odd one in the small family of twenty. Its side chain loops back and fastens to its own backbone, so the molecule cannot lie straight. It bends. It introduces a kink. It is the amino acid that lets collagen turn corners, that holds the curve in skin and tendon and the inner lining of every vessel.

There is a teaching in that, lower down than any teaching about family. The chemistry of this code is built on a thing that refuses the straight line. The bend is what gives the tissue its hold. Without the kink, nothing curves around anything else. Nothing cradles. The body simply does not know how to make a soft enclosing shape out of straight molecules. It needs the one that turns. The code runs all the way down to this: the bodily fact that what binds is not the strong straight thing, but the thing humble enough to bend back toward itself and stay.
